description: Design logic circuits from a written spec and convert any gate system to NAND gates only.
content_html:
From Problem Statement to Logic Circuit

Logic design starts with a written specification — a statement describing exactly when the output should be Logic 1. Your job is to translate that statement into a truth table, extract a Boolean expression, and select the gates to build it. This three-step pipeline is tested in nearly every exam paper and is the foundation of all digital design work.

Once you can design with standard gates, you will learn the most important conversion skill in this unit: replacing every gate in a circuit with NAND-only implementation. This matters because NAND gates are universal — any logic function can be built from them. In practice, a designer who needs only one type of IC can buy a single 4-NAND chip (such as the CMOS 4011) and implement any function without stocking multiple gate types.

Step 1 — Design from a Specification

Consider a burglar alarm that should activate (output = 1) when the door sensor (A) is 1 and the motion sensor (B) is 1, or when the panic button (C) is pressed (1). The Boolean expression is \(Q = A \cdot B + C\). The truth table has 8 rows (three inputs, \(2^3 = 8\) combinations). Rows where A=1 and B=1, or C=1, give Q=1.

The gate realisation needs an AND gate (inputs A and B) feeding into an OR gate alongside input C. This is a standard sum of products form. Most combinational logic specifications can be written as a sum of products, making the gate selection straightforward.

Key Fact

The three steps for logic design: (1) write the truth table from the specification; (2) write the Boolean expression from the rows where Q=1; (3) select the gates that match the expression. Every logic design question on the exam follows this pipeline.

NAND Equivalents for Each Gate

The conversion to NAND-only is systematic. There is a known NAND equivalent for every standard gate. Learn these four equivalents and the conversion becomes mechanical:

NAND equivalents for standard logic gates
Standard gateNAND-only equivalentBoolean check
NOT (A) One NAND gate with both inputs tied to A \(\overline{A \cdot A} = \overline{A}\)
AND (A, B) One NAND followed by a tied-input NOT-NAND on its output \(\overline{\overline{A \cdot B}} = A \cdot B\)
OR (A, B) NOT-NAND each input separately, then combine with a third NAND \(\overline{\overline{A} \cdot \overline{B}} = A + B\)
NOR (A, B) OR-equivalent (three NANDs) followed by a tied-input NOT-NAND \(\overline{A + B}\)
Key Fact

The three most important NAND equivalents: NOT = one NAND with inputs tied together; AND = NAND followed by a tied-input NAND on its output; OR = NOT-NAND each input separately, then combine with a third NAND.

The Conversion Algorithm — Three Steps

When the exam asks you to convert a circuit to NAND only, follow this exact sequence:

Step 1 — Redraw with NAND equivalents. Replace each gate in the original circuit with its NAND equivalent from the table above. The intermediate circuit will now contain only NAND gates — but it may have more gates than necessary.

Step 2 — Identify back-to-back (double inversion) pairs. Scan the circuit for any point where a NAND output connects directly into the “both-inputs-tied” (NOT-configured) NAND input. Two inversions in a row cancel out: \(\overline{\overline{X}} = X\). Mark these pairs.

Step 3 — Cancel the back-to-back pairs. Remove both back-to-back NANDs and connect the wire directly. This simplifies the circuit and reduces gate count. The resulting circuit is the minimal NAND-only implementation.

Original circuit: AND gate (inputs A, B) feeding an OR gate alongside input C. Boolean: \(Q = AB + C\).

Step 1 — Replace the AND gate with NAND(A,B) followed by a tied-input NAND on its output. Replace the OR gate with a NOT-NAND on each of its inputs, then combine those outputs with a third NAND. Intermediate circuit has 5 NAND gates.

Step 2 — The output of the tied-input NAND after the AND gate feeds directly into the tied-input NAND on the OR-equivalent side. These two are back-to-back — double inversion identified.

Step 3 — Cancel: remove those two back-to-back NANDs and connect the NAND(A,B) output directly to the input of the final NAND. Final circuit uses 3 NAND gates: NAND(A,B), NOT-NAND(C,C), NAND of those two results. Boolean check: \(\overline{\overline{AB} \cdot \overline{C}} = AB + C\) — correct by De Morgan.

Double Inversion and De Morgan’s Theorem

Double inversion is the key simplification step. Any time a signal passes through two inverters in a row (or two tied-input NANDs), both can be removed. This is the step that students most commonly miss in the exam — they draw a correct but bloated NAND circuit with redundant gate pairs still in place.

De Morgan’s theorem states \(\overline{A} \cdot \overline{B} = \overline{A + B}\), which rearranges to show that NAND of the complements equals the NOR, and \(\overline{\overline{A} \cdot \overline{B}} = A + B\), confirming the OR equivalent. You do not need to prove De Morgan in the exam — apply it to verify your NAND conversion is correct.

Logic ICs: The CMOS 4000 Series

In practice, logic gates are packaged as CMOS 4000 series ICs. Each IC package contains several identical gates sharing a power supply pin (VDD) and a ground pin (VSS). The 4011 contains four two-input NAND gates; the 4001 contains four two-input NOR gates. When using these ICs, unused inputs must be tied to Logic 0 or Logic 1 (not left floating) to prevent unpredictable switching.

A 14-pin dual in-line (DIL) package has 7 pins on each side. The notch or dot marks pin 1 (top left). Pins are numbered anticlockwise from pin 1. For a quad 2-input NAND (4011): pin 14 is VDD (supply), pin 7 is VSS (ground). The four gates share these supply pins — you only need to connect VDD and VSS once for all four gates.

In exam questions showing a pinout, identify the gate inputs and outputs by their pin numbers. A question might ask you to state which pins to connect to implement a specific logic function using available gates on the IC. Always check that you are using a gate that is on the IC — examiners have penalised students who used the wrong gate type for the IC shown.
exam_tip_html: NAND-only conversion is worth 6 marks on the paper and is consistently the weakest-answered question every year. Use the three-step method every time: (1) replace each gate with its NAND equivalent; (2) mark back-to-back NANDs (double inversions); (3) cancel them. Drawing a bloated 5-gate answer when the correct answer is 3 gates drops you to a partial mark band. For logic design questions, write the truth table before attempting the Boolean expression — students who jump straight to the expression miss rows and get the wrong gate combination.
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • Logic design follows three steps: write the truth table from the specification, extract the Boolean expression from the rows where Q=1, then select gates. Most expressions can be written in sum-of-products form.
  • Any standard gate can be replaced with NAND gates: NOT = tied-input NAND; AND = NAND then NOT-NAND; OR = two NOT-NANDs feeding a NAND. After substitution, cancel back-to-back (double-inversion) NAND pairs.
  • Logic ICs used in this course are CMOS 4000 series. Unused inputs must be tied to a defined logic level — never left floating. The supply pin VDD and ground pin VSS are shared by all gates in the package.

practice_questions.text:
Which one of the following is the correct NAND-only equivalent of a NOT gate?
A) A NAND gate with inputs A and B
B) A NAND gate with both inputs tied together to signal A
C) Two NAND gates in series, each with separate inputs
D) A NAND gate with input A and input B permanently at Logic 0
practice_questions.marks: B) A NAND gate with both inputs tied together to signal A [1 mark]

practice_questions.text: State what is meant by 'double inversion' in a NAND-only circuit and explain why back-to-back NAND pairs can be removed.
practice_questions.marks:
Double inversion is when a signal passes through two NOT operations (inverters) in succession. [1 mark]
Two inversions cancel because NOT(NOT(X)) = X, so the signal is unchanged and the two gates add no function to the circuit. [1 mark]

practice_questions.text:
A logic system has the Boolean expression Q = A AND B OR C (Q = AB + C).
(a) Complete the truth table for this expression.
(b) Identify the gates needed to implement this circuit directly.
practice_questions.marks:
(a) Correct 8-row truth table with Q = 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1 for rows 000 through 111 [2 marks: 1 mark for 5 or more correct rows, 2 marks for all 8 correct]
(b) One AND gate (inputs A and B) and one OR gate combining the AND output with C [2 marks: 1 per gate correctly identified]

practice_questions.text: Convert the following circuit to a NAND-only implementation. The circuit consists of an AND gate (inputs A, B) whose output feeds an OR gate alongside input C. Show all steps: NAND equivalents, identification of double inversions, and the simplified circuit.
practice_questions.marks:
Step 1 — Replace AND(A,B) with NAND(A,B) followed by tied-input NAND; replace OR with NOT-NANDs on each input then a combining NAND. [2 marks for correct equivalents shown]
Step 2 — Identifies the tied-input NAND on the AND output is back-to-back with the tied-input NAND on the C-input side of the OR equivalent. [1 mark]
Step 3 — Cancels the back-to-back pair, resulting in three NAND gates: NAND(A,B), NAND(C,C), NAND of those two outputs. [2 marks for correct simplified circuit]
Boolean verification or correct gate count stated. [1 mark]

practice_questions.text: Design a logic sub-system for a greenhouse alarm that outputs Logic 1 when the temperature sensor (T) is Logic 1 OR the humidity sensor (H) is Logic 1, but NOT when both are Logic 1 simultaneously. Write the truth table, Boolean expression, and specify the required gates.
practice_questions.marks:
Truth table (4 rows): TH=00 Q=0; TH=01 Q=1; TH=10 Q=1; TH=11 Q=0. [1 mark]
Boolean expression: Q = T.NOT(H) + NOT(T).H (exclusive OR expression). [1 mark]
Gates required: two NOT gates (one on T, one on H), two AND gates for each product term, one OR gate combining them. [2 marks: 1 per correct gate type identified]
Alternatively accepts XOR gate with justification. [1 mark]

practice_questions.text: A student converts a two-gate circuit (AND then OR) to NAND-only but does not cancel the back-to-back NAND pairs. Their final circuit has five NAND gates. A second student correctly cancels the double inversions and produces a three-gate circuit. Both circuits produce the same outputs. Evaluate which design is preferable for use in a real electronic product and explain why, with reference to IC gate count, cost, and any practical wiring considerations.
practice_questions.type: 8 marks — Extended Response: Circuit Analysis and Evaluation
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering: Clearly argues the three-gate design is preferable on multiple grounds. Each additional NAND gate requires IC pins; five gates may require a second IC while three gates fit on one 4011 with a spare gate. Fewer ICs means lower cost, smaller PCB footprint, fewer solder joints, and higher reliability. Notes that unused gates on a CMOS IC must have their inputs tied to a defined level, adding wiring complexity when a second IC is needed. Conclusion explicitly links fewer gates to lower cost and more reliable product.
Secure: Identifies that fewer gates may fit on one IC versus two, gives a cost or reliability argument, mentions unused inputs needing to be tied. May omit PCB footprint or solder joint detail.
Developing: Correctly states the three-gate design uses fewer components and is cheaper, but explanation of IC count or practical wiring is incomplete.
Emerging: States the three-gate design is better without technical justification.

knowledge_checks.q: How many NAND gates are needed to build a NAND-only equivalent of a two-input AND gate?
What should be done with unused inputs on a CMOS 4000 series logic IC?
options: Connected to the output of another gate

knowledge_checks.q: When converting to NAND-only, back-to-back NAND pairs can be removed because two consecutive _____ cancel each other out.
The CMOS 4011 IC contains four two-input _____ gates in a single 14-pin package.
Match each standard gate to its NAND-only equivalent description:
right: Two NOT-NANDs on each input, outputs combined by a third NAND
One NAND with both inputs tied to the same signal
One NAND followed by a tied-input NAND on its output

flashcard_questions.q: What are the three steps of the logic design process?
flashcard_questions.a: Write truth table, extract Boolean expression, select gates.

flashcard_questions.q: What is sum-of-products form in Boolean algebra?
flashcard_questions.a: Output written as OR of AND terms, e.g. Q = AB + C.

flashcard_questions.q: How do you build a NOT gate from a single NAND gate?
flashcard_questions.a: Tie both inputs of the NAND together to the same signal A.

flashcard_questions.q: How many NAND gates are needed to make an AND gate?
flashcard_questions.a: Two: one NAND(A,B) followed by a tied-input NAND on its output.

flashcard_questions.q: How many NAND gates are needed to make an OR gate?
flashcard_questions.a: Three: a NOT-NAND on each input, then a third NAND combining them.
Two consecutive NOT operations on the same signal, which cancel to give the original.

flashcard_questions.q: Why can back-to-back NAND pairs be removed in a NAND-only circuit?
flashcard_questions.a: Because NOT(NOT(X)) = X: the two inversions cancel each other.
A 14-pin IC containing four two-input NAND gates.

flashcard_questions.q: What must be done with unused gate inputs on a CMOS 4000 series IC?
flashcard_questions.a: Tied to a defined logic level (Logic 0 or Logic 1) — never left floating.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is a NAND gate described as a universal gate?
flashcard_questions.a: Because any logic function can be built using only NAND gates.

flashcard_questions.q: On a 14-pin CMOS IC, which pins are power supply (V_DD) and ground (V_SS)?
flashcard_questions.a: Pin 14 is V_DD (supply); pin 7 is V_SS (ground).

flashcard_questions.q: What does De Morgan's theorem say about NOT(A) AND NOT(B)?
flashcard_questions.a: NOT(A) AND NOT(B) = NOT(A OR B): the NAND of complements equals the NOR.

glossary_terms.definition: Replacing every standard logic gate in a circuit with an equivalent combination of NAND gates, so the circuit uses only NAND gates throughout.
A Boolean expression written as the OR of one or more AND terms, each AND term being a product of input variables or their complements.
The principle that two consecutive NOT operations cancel each other: double inversion of a signal returns the original value.
A family of CMOS integrated circuits, numbered 4000 onwards, containing two to four logic gates in a single package.
